title: Banned strcpy() in production C: coap/checkin.c, coap/slot_claim_settings.c (spec appendix-c R-APPC-014)
description: spec/appendix-c-safety.md R-APPC-014 (Coding Rules, CERT C subset): 'Never use these functions: strcpy, strcat, sprintf, gets.' Sweep classification: divergent. Production-code violations: lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/checkin.c:1670 strcpy(rc->id, req.id) and :1673 strcpy(rc->creator, creator) (into fixed struct fields; creator is strlen-guarded here, req.id validation is upstream), and lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/slot_claim_settings.c:249 strcpy(name, SETTINGS_ROOT "/") (constant prefix into caller buffer). Test code additionally uses strcpy/strcat freely (lichen/tests/checkin_rollcall/main.c:389+, lichen/tests/slot_claim_settings/main.c:179-180) — lower stakes. No sprintf/gets anywhere in lichen/ or firmware/ (word-boundary rg clean). Suggested placement: replace with bounded copies (memcpy with explicit size against sizeof field, or a strlcpy-style helper) in lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/checkin.c and slot_claim_settings.c; optional test sweep. Full row in docs/spec-coverage.md (spec/appendix-c-safety.md sweep 2026-08-31).
close_reason: RE-CLOSE (store reverted the earlier close; see bd8h — 3rd occurrence of lost writes).
